G9500.definition: of three stories   or  floors  , (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G9501.definition: to furnish the oar with its thong  : Mid., τροποῦτο κώπην ἀμφὶ σκαλμόν  fastened his   oar  by its thong   round the thole, (Aeschulus Tragicus):—;Pass., of the oar,  to be furnished with its thong  , (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

G9503.definition:
τροφο-φορέω , -ῶ, 
 [in LXX:  Deu.1:31  (נָשָׂא),  2Ma.7:27  * ;] 
to nourish (Hesych.),  bear like a nurse  (R, mg., bare he them as a nursing-father): with accusative of person(s),  Act.13:18 , T, Tr., R, mg. (WH, R, txt., τροποφορέω, which see).†
 (AS)

G9506.definition:
1.  a vintage, harvest  , (Plutarch) 
2.  the time thereof, the harvest   or  vintage  , (Thucydides) (ML)

G9508.definition:
1.  to bore, pierce through  , (Odyssey by Homer):—;Pass., τὰ ὦτα τετρυπημένος  having   one's ears  pierced for earrings  , (Xenophon Historicus); ψῆφος τετρυπημένη the pebble of condemnation  which had a hole in it  , (Aeschines Orator) 
2. τρ. τῷ ποδὶ τὴν βελόνην  to force   the point  through   the foot, [  variant  dates Anthology Palantina   (ML)

G9510.definition: 1.  delicate, dainty  , (Euripides), etc.:—; τὸ τρυφερόν  effeminacy  , ἐς τὸ τρυφερώτερον  to more effeminate habits  , (Thucydides):—; neuter  as  adverb , τρυφερόν  voluptuously  , (Aristophanes Comicus); τρ. λαλεῖν to speak  softly  , (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus) (ML)

G9512.definition: a hole formed by gnawing, a mouse's hole  , (Batrachomyomachia) (ML)

G9513.definition:
1.  to make knobby  :—;Pass., ῥόπαλα σιδήρῳ τετυλωμένα clubs  knobbed   with iron, (Herdotus Historicus) 
2.  to make callous  , (Xenophon Historicus):—;Pass.  to be callous  , (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus) (ML)

G9515.definition:
1.  a kettledrum  , such as was used especially in the worship of Cybele, (Herdotus Historicus) 
2.  a drum-stick  : generally,  a staff, cudgel  , (Aristophanes Comicus) 
3. in  Virgil    tympana   are  wheels of solid wood.   (ML)

G9517.definition:
1.  kingly power, sovereignty  , (Pindar), attic; τ. ὑμῶν  lordship   over you, (Demosthenes Orator) 
3.  plural , αἱ τυραννίδες, = οἱ τύραννοι, (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G9519.definition:
1.  the good which man obtains   τυγχάνει);  by the favour of the gods, good fortune, luck, success  , (Theognis Elegiacus), etc.; σὺν τύχῃ (Sophocles Tragicus); θείᾳ τύχῃ, Lat.  divinitus , (Herdotus Historicus), etc.:—; hence Τύχη was deified, like Lat.  Fortuna , Τύχη Σώτειρα (Pindar); T. Σωτήρ (Aeschulus Tragicus) 
2. generally,  fortune, chance  , good or bad, in  singular  and  plural , (Herdotus Historicus), attic 
3. rarely of positive  ill fortune  , ἢν χρήσωνται τύχῃ, i. e. if they are killed, (Euripides); τύχῃ  by ill-luck  , (Antipho Orator) 
4. especially, ἀγαθὴ τ. (Aeschulus Tragicus), etc.; in  dative  ἀγαθῇ τύχῃ  "in God's name, "   (Demosthenes Orator), etc.; by crasis, τύχἀγαθῇ (Aristophanes Comicus);—;this formula was also introduced into treaties, like Lat.  quod felix faustumque sit , Λάχης εἶπε, τύχῃ ἀγαθῇ τῶν Ἀθηναίων ποιεῖσθαι τὴν ἐκεχειρίαν Decret. in (Thucydides):—;so ἐπ᾽ ἀγαθῇ τύχῃ (Aristophanes Comicus), etc. 
5. Adverbial usages, τύχῃ  by chance  , Lat.  forte , forte fortuna, (Sophocles Tragicus), etc.; ἀπὸ τύχης (Aristotle Philosopher); ἐκ τύχης (Plato Philosophus); διὰ τύχην (Isocrates Orator), etc.; κατὰ τύχην (Thucydides), etc. 
6.  a chance, hap, accident  , (Aeschulus Tragicus), etc.; τῆς τύχης, τὸ ἐμὲ τυχεῖν . . !  what a piece of ill-luck  , that . . ! (Xenophon Historicus); mostly of  mishaps, misfortunes  , (Aeschulus Tragicus), etc. (ML)

G9520.definition: the hyaena  , an animal of the dog kind, with a bristly mane like a hog (whence the name), (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G9521.definition: given to wantonness, wanton, insolent, outrageous  , (Plato Philosophus), etc.:—; τὸ ὑβριστικόν  an insolent disposition  , (Xenophon Historicus):—; adverb  -κῶς, (Plato Philosophus);  comparative  -ώτερον, (Demosthenes Orator) (ML)

G9523.definition:
1.  health, soundness   of body, Lat.  salus , (Herdotus Historicus), attic:—; plural  ὑγίειαι,  healthy states   or  conditions  , (Plato Philosophus) 
2. of the mind, ὑ. φρενῶν  soundness   of mind, (Aeschulus Tragicus) (ML)

G9525.definition: to wet, moisten  , (Euripides): of a river,  to water   a country, (Euripides) (ML)

G9528.definition: to draw, fetch   or  carry water  , (Odyssey by Homer):—;Mid.  to draw water for oneself, fetch water  , πολῖται (Odyssey by Homer), attic (ML)

G9530.definition:
1.  carrying water  , (Plutarch) 
2. as  Substantive , ὑδρ.,  a water-carrier  , (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G9531.definition: of   or  belonging to swine  , ὑεία κοιλία  pig's   tripe, (Aristophanes Comicus):—; θηρίον ὕ., as a type of brutish ignorance, (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

G9533.definition:
1.  to bark, bay, howl  , of dogs, (Iliad by Homer); of hounds,  to give tongue  , (Xenophon Historicus) 
2.  metaphorically , κραδίη ὑλακτεῖ  howls for rage  , (Odyssey by Homer); with  accusative   cognate   to yell forth bold and shameless words  , (Sophocles Tragicus); ἄμους᾽ ὑλακτῶν  howling   his uncouth songs, (Euripides) 
3.  transitive   to bark at  , τινά (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

G9534.definition:
1.  woody, wooded  , (Thucydides); τὰ ὑλώδη  wooded ground  , (Xenophon Historicus) 
2.  turbid, muddy  , (Plutarch) (ML)

G9536.definition:
1.  to sing a hymn   or  song of praise  : generally,  to sing  , ὑμν. θρῆνον (Aeschulus Tragicus) 
2. = χρησμῳδέω, (Euripides)[ ῦ in (Aeschulus Tragicus)] (ML)

G9537.definition:
1. as  Substantive , ἐν ὑπαίθρῳ,  entry Dio, in the open air  , (Xenophon Historicus) 
2. τὰ ὕπαιθρα,  the field, the open country  , (Polybius Historicus) (ML)

G9538.definition:
1. like Lat. summus for  supremus, the highest, uppermost  , of Zeus, ὕπατος κρειόντων, θεῶν ὕπ., (Homer); οἱ ὕπατοι  the gods above  , Lat.  superi , opposite to οἱ χθόνιοι, Lat.  inferi , (Aeschulus Tragicus); ὕπατός τις some  god above  , (Aeschulus Tragicus) 
2. simply of Place, ἐν πυρῇ ὑπάτῃ  on the very top   of the funeral pile, (Iliad by Homer) 
3. of Time,  last  , Lat.  supremus , (Sophocles Tragicus) 
5. with  genitive , like the  preposition  ὑπό, ὕπατος χώρας  supreme over   the land, (Aeschulus Tragicus); ὕπατοι λεχέων  high above   the nest, (Aeschulus Tragicus) 
6. as  Substantive , ὕπατος, the Roman  consul  , (Polybius Historicus), etc. (ML)

G9546.definition: to set up, prop up, support

G9548.definition:
1. much like ὑπερηνορέων  overweening, arrogant  , (Iliad by Homer) 
2.  transitive   to treat disdainfully  , (Lucian) (ML)

G9551.definition:
1. Dep. 
2.  to lie   or  be situate above  , (Isocrates Orator) 
3.  to be postponed  , (Lucian) (ML)

G9554.definition:
1.  exceeding long  , (Aeschulus Tragicus); ἡ βασιλέος χεὶρ ὑπ. the king's arm is  very long, reaches very far  , (Herdotus Historicus) 
2.  exceeding high  , of mountains, (Herdotus Historicus) 
3. ὑπερμάκης βοά a cry  exceeding loud  , (Pindar) (ML)

G9557.definition:
ὑπερ-οράω , see: ὑπερεῖδον.
  ὑπερ-εῖδον , aor. 
 [in LXX for עָלַם hi., מַעַל, etc. ;] 
 to overlook : with accusative of thing(s),  Act.17:30  
 (AS)

G9559.definition:
1.  to set higher, erect  , [  variant  dates Anthology Palantina   
2.  to set on the other side, carry over  , (Plutarch) 
3. in Mid.  to hold over  , so as to protect, [  variant  dates Anthology Palantina   
4.  metaphorically , παντὶ θεὸν ὑπερτιθέμεν  to set   God  over   all, (Pindar) 
5.  to communicate   a thing to another, ὑπερετίθεα (ionic  imperfect  for -ετίθην); τὰ ἔμελλον ποιήσειν (Herdotus Historicus):—;so in Mid., especially in order to ask advice, (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G9561.definition:
1.  to bear   or  carry over   a place, ὑπ. τὸν ἰσθμὸν τὰς ναῦς (Thucydides):—;Pass., [ αἱ ναῦς] αἱ ὑπερενεχθεῖσαι τὸν ἰσθμόν (Thucydides) 
2.  intransitive   to rise above, to surpass, excel, have the advantage over  , τινός τινι one in a thing, (Herdotus Historicus); also with  accusative  pro  genitive , ὑπερφέρεις τόλμῃ τόλμαν (Euripides):  absolute   to excel, have preeminence  , (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G9565.definition:
1.  liable to give account for   one's  administration   of an office,  accountable, responsible  , (Herdotus Historicus), etc.:—; ὑπεύθυνοι, οἱ, at Athens, magistrates who  had to submit their accounts   to public auditors  λογισταί); (Aristophanes Comicus), etc. 
2. with  genitive   responsible for  , ὑπ. ἀρχῆς ἑτέρας quoted in (Demosthenes Orator); of slaves, σῶμα ὑπ. ἀδικημάτων their body is  liable for   their misdeeds, i. e. they  must pay for   them with their body, (Demosthenes Orator) 
3. with  dative   responsible to   another,  dependent on   them, Lat.  obnoxius , (Demosthenes Orator) (ML)

G9566.definition:
1.  the body of rowers and sailors, the ship's crew  , (Thucydides), etc. 
2.  service  , (Aristophanes Comicus), etc. (ML)

G9567.definition: to put to sleep  :—; Pass.  to fall asleep, sleep  , (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G9569.definition: to look up from under   the brows  at, glance at, to look askance at, eye suspiciously   or  angrily  , Lat.  limis oculis suspicere , (Plato Philosophus); also ὑπ. ἐλεεινά  to cast   piteous  glances  , [  variant  dates Anthology Palantina  :—;Pass.  to be looked at with suspicion  , (Euripides) (ML)

G9571.definition: a garment under a coat of mail  , (Plutarch) (ML)

G9573.definition:
1.  to burn by applying fire below  , (Herdotus Historicus):  to offer secret sacrifices  , (Aeschulus Tragicus) 
2.  to light under  , (Lucian) (ML)

G9576.definition:
1.  to lie under   or  beneath  , (Iliad by Homer); with  dative , (Plato Philosophus) 
2. in various  metaphorically  senses, 
3.  to be put under   the eyes or mind, i. e.  to be submitted   or  proposed to one  , (Pindar); αἱ ὑποκείμεναι ἐλπίδες one's  present   hopes, (Demosthenes Orator); ὑπόκειταί μοι ὅτι . .  I have laid down the rule  , that . ., (Herdotus Historicus) 
4.  to be laid down   or  assumed as an hypothesis  , (Plato Philosophus), etc.; τούτων ὑποκειμένων = Lat.  his positis , (Plato Philosophus);  impersonal , ὑπόκειται  a rule is laid down  , (Demosthenes Orator); ὑποκείσθω ὅτι . .  let it be granted   that . ., (Aristotle Philosopher) 
5.  to be suggested  , (Herdotus Historicus) 
6.  to be left at bottom, left remaining  , (Thucydides) 
7.  to be subject to, submit to  , τινι (Plato Philosophus):  absolute   to be submissive  , (Plato Philosophus) 
8.  to be left behind in pledge, to be pledged   or  mortgaged  , τινος  for   a certain sum, (Demosthenes Orator), etc.; ὑποκείμενοι, of persons,  bound for payment   of a sum of money, (Demosthenes Orator) 
9.  to underlie  , as a substratum, (Plato Philosophus), etc. 
10.  to be subordinate  , (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

G9577.definition:
ὑπό-λειμμα  
 (WH, -λιμμα, see their  App. , 154), -τος, τό, [in LXX chiefly for שָׁאַר ;] 
 a remnant :  Rom.9:27  (Arist., al.; cf. κατάλειμμα).†
 (AS)

G9578.definition:
1.  left behind, staying behind  , (Herdotus Historicus); οἱ ὑπ.  those who remained alive  , (Herdotus Historicus) 
2. of things, ὑπ. τὸ βάραθρον γίγνεται the pit  still remains  , (Aristophanes Comicus); ὅσα ἦν ὑπ. all that  remained to be done  , (Thucydides) (ML)

G9580.definition:
1.  to loosen beneath   or  below  , ὑπέλυσε γυῖα  made   his limbs  give way under him  , (Iliad by Homer):—;Pass., γυῖα ὑπέλυντο (Iliad by Homer) 
2.  to loose from under   the yoke, (Homer):—;  to loose from bonds  , (Odyssey by Homer); in Mid., τὸν ὑπελύσαο δεσμῶν thou  didst free   him from bonds  by stealth  , (Iliad by Homer) 
3.  to untie   a person's sandals  from under   his feet,  take off   his shoes, (Aeschulus Tragicus):—;Mid.  to take off one's   sandals or shoes, or  to have   them  taken off  , (Aristophanes Comicus) 
4. with  accusative  pers.  to unshoe   him,  take off   his  shoes  , (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

G9581.definition:
1.  a remembrance, memorial  , (Thucydides), etc. 
2.  a note, memorandum  , (Demosthenes Orator):—;in  plural   memoranda, notes, minutes  , Lat.  commentarii , (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

G9584.definition: to prick   or  sting underneath  : generally,  to sting  , (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus) (ML)

G9585.definition:
1.  to fall under   or  down, to sink in  , (Plutarch) 
2.  to fall down before   any one, with  accusative , (Plato Philosophus): —;hence,  to be subject   to him,  fall under   his power, (Isocrates Orator); of a flatterer,  to cringe to  , τινί (Demosthenes Orator); with  accusative  ὑποπεσὼν τὸν δεσπότην (Aristophanes Comicus) 
3.  to fall behind   another, (Demosthenes Orator) 
4.  to get in under   or  among  , (Thucydides) 
5. of accidents,  to happen, fall out  , (Isocrates Orator) 
6. of persons,  to fall under   a punishment, with  dative , (Plutarch) 
7. of places,  to lie under   or  below  , with  dative , (Polybius Historicus) (ML)

G9586.definition:
1.  to be suspicious  , (Xenophon Historicus); also, ὑπ. εἴς τινα  to have suspicions   of him, (Thucydides) 
2.  to suspect, guess, suppose  , (Xenophon Historicus) 
3.  transitive   to suspect, hold in suspicion  , (Sophocles Tragicus); ὑπ. τινὰ εἴς τι of something, (Herdotus Historicus), etc.:—;Pass.  to be suspected, mistrusted  , (Thucydides);  impersonal , ὡς ὑπωπτεύετο as  was generally suspected  , (Xenophon Historicus) 
4. with  accusative  pers. et  infinitive   to suspect that  , (Herdotus Historicus), etc. 
5. with  accusative  rei,  to look suspiciously on  , (Thucydides):—;but also, ὑπ. τι  to suspect   something, (Euripides) 
from ὑπόπτης (ML)

G9588.definition:
1.  to trip up one's heels, upset  , Lat.  supplantare , (Demosthenes Orator) 
2.  metaphorically , ὑπ. καὶ ἀνατρέπων (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

G9594.definition: rendering service, serviceable, promoting, conducive to   a thing, with  dative , (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

G9595.definition: a light shewing through a small hole: a narrow opening  , (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G9597.definition:
1.  under the hand, in hand  , (Odyssey by Homer) 
2. of persons,  under   any one's  hand, under command, subject  , τινι (Herdotus Historicus), etc.; λαβεῖν τινα ὑποχείριον to get  into one's power  , (Euripides); ἔχειν τινὰ ὑπ. (Thucydides) (ML)

G9599.definition:
1.  indebted, in debt  , (Aristophanes Comicus); ὑπ. τινος his  debtor  , (Plutarch) 
2. of property,  involved  , Lat.  obaeratus , (Demosthenes Orator) 
3. with  genitive , ὑπ. φιλίας  bound by ties of   friendship, (Plutarch) (ML)
